exits.label: Stairs
exits.text: The stairs climb back toward the sour kitchen light.

verbs.look: The stairs climb back to the kitchen. The light up there looks sick, but at least it is light.
verbs.pickup: I am not taking the stairs with me. The landlord can keep them.

use.text: I climb back toward the kitchen. The basement keeps breathing behind me.

action.text: I climb back toward the kitchen. The basement keeps breathing behind me.

exits.label: Garage Door
exits.text: The door drags across the concrete. Somewhere above, something answers.

verbs.look: The garage door is old metal and bad manners. Opening it will not be quiet.
verbs.pickup: No. Too big, too metal, too landlord-shaped.

use.text: The garage door drags across the concrete. Somewhere above, something answers.

action.text: The garage door drags across the concrete. Somewhere above, something answers.

verbs.look: A gasoline can, heavy with exactly the kind of hope that ruins your posture.
verbs.use: I need to carry it to the car, not pour it on the basement like an idiot poet.

onEnter.text: The basement air tastes like wet cardboard, old wire, and the promise of something heavy to carry back.

#0000ff.label: Stairs
#0000ff.text: I climb back toward the kitchen. The dark below does not complain when I leave.

verbs.look: The stairs climb back to the kitchen. The light up there looks sick, but at least it is light.
verbs.pickup: I am not taking the stairs with me. The landlord can keep them.

use.text: I climb back toward the kitchen. The dark below does not complain when I leave.

#00ff00.label: Shelves
#00ff00.text: A flathead screwdriver slides from behind a row of dead paint cans. Small miracle, cheap handle.
#00ff00.repeatText: Rows of jars, tins, and forgotten supplies. The useful thing is already in my pocket.

verbs.look: Paint cans, jars, and one useful shape half-hidden behind them. The shelf is pretending not to help.

pickup.text: I take the flathead screwdriver. Small miracle, cheap handle.
pickup.repeatText: Rows of jars, tins, and forgotten supplies. The useful thing is already in my pocket.

verbs.use: I rattle the shelf. It answers with dust and nothing revolutionary.

#00ffff.label: Sink
#00ffff.text: A stained utility sink squats under the pipes. Whatever dried in it did not go quietly.

verbs.look: A stained utility sink squats under the pipes. Whatever dried in it did not go quietly.
verbs.pickup: I am not picking up the sink. Plumbing is counter-revolutionary today.
verbs.use: No water. Just pipe groans and insult.

#ff8800.label: Crate
#ff8800.text: The crate complains loudly. Inside: two shotgun shells. A generous apocalypse would have left more.

verbs.look: The crate looks loose, noisy, and maybe worth the trouble. Terrible combination.

pickup.text: The crate complains loudly. Inside: two shotgun shells. A generous apocalypse would have left more.

verbs.use: I pry at the crate. It complains loudly enough to make the basement feel crowded.

#ffff00.label: Breaker Box
#ffff00.text: Behind the cracked panel, I find a fuse that somehow survived the building better than the people did.
#ffff00.repeatText: The breaker box is empty now. Its switches stare back like bad teeth.

verbs.look: The breaker box has one lonely useful part left inside. It looks like it knows it is important.

pickup.text: Behind the cracked panel, I find a fuse that somehow survived the building better than the people did.
pickup.repeatText: The breaker box is empty now. Its switches stare back like bad teeth.

verbs.use: I flip a dead switch. Nothing wakes up except the bad feeling.

#808080.label: Chest
#808080.text: A small chest waits on the floor, too neat for this room and therefore suspicious.

verbs.look: A small chest waits on the floor, too neat for this room and therefore suspicious.
verbs.pickup: It is heavier than it looks and less useful than it wants to be.
verbs.use: It sticks. Whatever is inside can keep lying to itself.

#ff00ff.label: Brooms
#ff00ff.text: A broom and mop lean together like exhausted witnesses.

verbs.look: A broom and mop lean together like exhausted witnesses.
verbs.pickup: A broom is not saving me tonight. Not unless the dead respect cleanliness.
verbs.use: I consider cleaning. The apocalypse considers laughing.

verbs.look: The gasoline can is tucked near the barrel, heavy and rude and necessary.
verbs.use: I need to bring the can to the car first.

verbs.look: The right-side crates hide the gasoline can like a bad secret with a handle.
verbs.use: I shift the crates just enough to regret having arms.
